title: M&M Financial Profit Climbs 61% Consolidated; Eternal Profit Surges 92% but Misses Estimates
excerpt: M&M Financial's consolidated Q2 profit rose to Rs 910.73 crore with improving asset quality, while Eternal's Rs 125 crore profit nearly doubled but fell short of the Rs 271 crore analysts expected as Blinkit expansion spending weighed.
body:
• M&M Financial Services' consolidated net profit climbed about 61% year on year to Rs 910.73 crore in Q2 FY27; standalone profit rose 55% to Rs 882 crore, with net interest income up 13.2% to Rs 2,391 crore.
  • Eternal, parent of Zomato and Blinkit, reported net profit up 92.3% to Rs 125 crore on revenue up 78% to Rs 24,138 crore — but missed the LSEG analyst estimate of Rs 271 crore as Blinkit expansion costs weighed.
  • Blinkit added 308 stores in the quarter to reach 2,751, and Eternal now targets 3,500 stores by March 2027 and around 5,000 by March 2028.
  • Eternal shares ended Wednesday 2.71% lower at Rs 311.75 despite the profit jump — for investors, the quarter's question is whether Blinkit's spending converts into durable margins.

Two very different profit stories led India's Q2 FY27 results on Wednesday. Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services delivered a clean beat powered by lending growth and better asset quality, while Eternal — the parent of Zomato and Blinkit — nearly doubled its profit yet still disappointed the Street, because the number came in well below what analysts had pencilled in.

M&M Financial: Profit Up 61% Consolidated

M&M Financial Services reported a 55% rise in standalone net profit to Rs 882 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, from Rs 569 crore a year earlier, with net interest income growing 13.2% to Rs 2,391 crore from Rs 2,112 crore, according to BusinessLine's Q2 results coverage. On a consolidated basis, net profit rose 60.9% to Rs 910.73 crore, with revenue from operations up 15.4% on a standalone basis to Rs 5,163.51 crore. Gross Stage-3 assets improved to 3.42% from 3.94% a year earlier, signalling cleaner loan quality alongside growth.

Eternal: Profit Up 92%, Estimates Missed

Eternal's consolidated net profit rose 92.3% to Rs 125 crore (1.25 billion rupees) in the September quarter, from Rs 65 crore a year earlier, but missed expectations as higher spending on expanding Blinkit weighed, according to Reuters. Analysts on average had expected a profit of Rs 271 crore, according to LSEG data compiled for Reuters.

The underlying growth was rapid. Operating revenue rose 78% year on year to Rs 24,138 crore, total expenses rose 75% to Rs 24,166 crore, and consolidated adjusted EBITDA almost tripled to Rs 666 crore, according to Inc42. Blinkit was the largest contributor: revenue up 94% to Rs 19,152 crore, net order value up 79.3% to Rs 20,940 crore, and adjusted EBITDA of Rs 184 crore against a Rs 156 crore loss a year ago. Zomato's food delivery net order value rose 21.5% to Rs 11,445 crore.

"There is still a lot of headroom. Restaurant food is a small part of how India eats. As cities grow, incomes rise and more young people live away from home, we think the food delivery market can keep compounding at 20%+ for many years."

— Deepinder Goyal, Founder, Eternal

Expansion Is the Strategy — and the Cost

Blinkit added 308 net new stores in the quarter, taking its network to 2,751. Eternal raised its target to cross 3,500 stores by March 2027 and reach around 5,000 by March 2028. CFO Akshant Goyal said new stores were meeting margin and payback expectations, with mature cities reporting adjusted EBITDA margins above 5%. The company's cash balance fell by Rs 1,813 crore to Rs 16,475 crore during the quarter, which it attributed to seasonal working capital, including building Blinkit inventory ahead of the festive season.

What's Next

For M&M Financial, investors will watch whether asset-quality gains hold as loan growth continues. For Eternal, the test is conversion: Blinkit's margin has now improved for six consecutive quarters, but the shares' 2.71% fall to Rs 311.75 on results day shows the market wants the expansion bill to shrink relative to revenue. The earnings season continues Thursday, with Swiggy, Colgate-Palmolive and Cyient among some 60 companies scheduled to report on October 22.
